of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

properties.description:
AQAPSR

The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality (ADEQ) has issued an
Ozone High Pollution Advisory for the Phoenix Metro Area on Tuesday.

This means that forecast weather conditions combined with existing
ozone levels are expected to result in local maximum 8-hour ozone
concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects
increase as air quality deteriorates.

Ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing difficulties
for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

You are urged to car pool, telecommute or use mass transit.
The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

For details on this High Pollution Advisory, visit the ADEQ internet
site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.

loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early

Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued August 24 at 4:56AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A wet system continues to move over the southern panhandle through
tonight, bringing an extended period of moderate to heavy rain for
the southern panhandle. Highest rain rates are expected through
this morning, perhaps around 0.2 to 0.4 inches per hour at times,
primarily for Ketchikan, Metlakatla, and Misty Fjords. Nearly 1.5 to
2.5 inches of rainfall has been observed since Sunday, with over 3
inches in some surrounding higher elevations. Through tonight, storm
event total rainfall of 2 to 3.5 inches is expected for low
elevation sites with up to 4.5 inches in the higher elevations.
There is moderate to high confidence for heavy rainfall over Annette
Island and Ketchikan with the highest rain totals near Misty Fjords.
Small streams and rivers are starting to show some rises, but no
river flooding is expected at this time. Ponding of water on some
roadways is likely.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.

* AFFECTED AREA...In California, Fire Weather Zones 280 and

California, this includes Scott Valley, Shasta Valley, and
the Klamath River Valley. In Oregon, this includes the

10 to 20 mph with gusts around 30 mph.

https://weather.gov/wrh/hazards?wfo=mfr
properties.instruction:
Follow all fire restrictions. You can find your county's
emergency sign up form as well as links to fire restrictions at
weather.gov/medford/wildfire. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Be sure you're signed up for your county's emergency alert
system. Familiarize yourself with your emergency plan and make
sure you listen to emergency services. Visit ready.gov/plan for
more information.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions
that promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-
threatening. This does not mean there is a fire. These conditions
are either occurring now or will begin soon. It is important to
have multiple ways to receive information from authorities.

evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat

properties.description:
ESFGUM

This Hydrologic Outlook is for Guam, Rota, Tinian, and Saipan.

A reinvigorated monsoon trough with a potential embedded tropical
disturbance that was previously expected to develop and bring periods
of heavy rainfall to the Marianas beginning Wednesday, has continued
to fallen behind. The mid to long-term model guidance continues to
show a downward trend in any potential cyclogenesis, with the
enhanced monsoon pattern now likely to fall apart over the next few
days, pushing back any potential heavy rainfall into the weekend,
potentially even into early next week as the col overhead lingers and
forces diffusive flow. Due to this uncertainty, this will be the last
Hydrologic Outlook issued for this rain event, unless conditions
warrant a new issuance in the coming days.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued August 23 at 1:53PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
ESFAFC

Locations:

* Yentna and Skwentna River basins
* Rivers, creeks, and streams with headwaters along the western
Talkeetna Mountains.

Timing:

* First Round - Late Monday Night through Wednesday Morning
* Second Round - Late Thursday Night through Saturday Evening

Rainfall:

* Widespread rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain is likely (70-80%)
across the Susitna Valley late Monday Night through Wednesday
morning. The highest amounts are very likely (80%-90%) to occur
from Petersville east to Talkeetna and along the Talkeetna
Mountains to Hatcher Pass.

* Additional widespread rainfall of 0.5 to 1.5 inches of rain is
likely (60-70%) across the Susitna Valley late Thursday Night
through Saturday evening. There is a low chance (20-30%) for
rainfall amounts higher than 1.5" across far northern and western
Susitna Valley.

* There is a chance (20-30%) of an additional 0.1 to 0.2 inches of
rain with any lingering scattered showers Wednesday afternoon and
evening.

Hydrologic Concerns:

* Expect sharp rises on many small streams and rivers, including the
Yentna at Lake Creek.

* Many lower locations along rivers such as gravel bars and other
spots popular for camping and recreating may become inundated with
water with rivers reaching bankfull conditions.

* Heavy rain may result in localized ponding in low-lying areas and
locations with poor drainage.

Next Steps:

* Residents along area streams as well as river users and recreators
should anticipate higher than normal water levels and are advised
to monitor weather and river forecasts.

* Send weather or flooding reports to inws.ncep.noaa.gov/report/ or
by calling 1-907-266-5127.

* Reports on river conditions may be sent to the river forecast
center by calling 1-907-266-5160.
